4.speaker: Symon Holl
4.text: "Mr. President. Where's the Vice President today?"

6.speaker: Player
6.text: "He's thinking very hard about what he did wrong."

7.speaker: Player
7.text: "I don't know. Have you seen him?"

11.speaker: Narrator
11.text: Symon's expression remained unchanged as he sat down to face me.

12.speaker: Symon Holl
12.text: "I just wanted to provide you with a few updates on the economy."

13.speaker: Symon Holl
13.text: "You may have noticed that the government budget is in need of a boost."

17.speaker: Symon Holl
17.text: "My ministry is therefore working on a bill that will increase the tax on tobacco products from 10 to 30 percent."

18.speaker: Symon Holl
18.text: "A similar bill is being drafted to introduce a 20 percent tax on alcohol."

19.speaker: Player
19.text: "Very good. Those are nasty vices anyway."

20.speaker: Player
20.text: "We can't tax people's booze and cigarettes. There'd be riots in the streets."

21.speaker: Player
21.text: "Interesting initiatives. But would the income we'd receive be worth the harm to Sordish businesses?"

22.speaker: Symon Holl
22.text: "Your public opinion would suffer. There's no getting around that."

23.speaker: Symon Holl
23.text: "Good question. The tax wouldn't apply to products designated for export, which would mitigate the damage somewhat."

24.speaker: Symon Holl
24.text: "Ordinarily, I'd advise against this kind of thing. But with our budget dipping into the red, any measure that would reverse our deficit is worth considering."

25.speaker: Symon Holl
25.text: "The government budget is currently healthy enough that we don't need to worry about introducing new tax measures."

26.speaker: Symon Holl
26.text: "Thankfully, tourism to Sordland is on the rise, so we can expect to see a healthy stream of income there."

33.speaker: Symon Holl
33.text: "Especially since the Sordish tourism industry has been stagnating."

34.speaker: Symon Holl
34.text: "Especially since our income from tourism is on the decline."

35.speaker: Symon Holl
35.text: "Especially since tourism to Sordland is on the rise."

42.speaker: Symon Holl
42.text: "Although it might be a nice fallback considering that the Sordish tourism industry has recently been stagnating due to stability issues."

43.speaker: Symon Holl
43.text: "Although it might be a nice fallback since our income from tourism is on the decline."
43.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_Tourism_Booming"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_Tourism_Average"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Bill_Turn02_TourismCulturalPreservation_Signed"] == true)

50.speaker: Symon Holl
50.text: "Our investment in cultural preservation failed to produce the intended effect, it seems."

51.speaker: Symon Holl
51.text: "Our investment in cultural preservation paid off, it seems."

52.speaker: Player
52.text: "Oh. I hope the increased threat of the BFF won't put a damper on that."

65.speaker: Player
65.text: "Wait until the world finds out we eliminated the BFF menace. They'll come in droves."
65.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_TourismAct"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Order_BFF_ThreatAlarming"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Order_BFF_ThreatEliminated"] == true)

66.speaker: Player
66.text: "Oh. I hope the increased threat of the BFF won't make matters worse."

67.speaker: Player
67.text: "Wait until the world finds out we've eliminated the BFF menace. They'll come in droves."
67.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Economy_TourismAct"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Order_BFF_ThreatAlarming"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Order_BFF_ThreatEliminated"])

68.speaker: Player
68.text: "That's good news. Thanks for telling me."

69.speaker: Player
69.text: "Who wouldn't want to visit Sordland? It's the best country in the world!"

71.speaker: Player
71.text: "Why wouldn't tourism be skyrocketing? Sordland is the best country in the world!"

73.speaker: Symon Holl
73.text: "The increased what!? I'd better have a talk with Lileas."

74.speaker: Symon Holl
74.text: "To live in, perhaps. But have you seen Lespia's beaches?"

75.speaker: Symon Holl
75.text: "To be fair, I never understood why anyone would want to vacation in Sordland when Lespia is right there."

76.speaker: Narrator
76.text: There was a knock on the door. Gus Manger strolled in and grabbed a seat.

77.speaker: Symon Holl
77.text: "I never quite understood why anyone would want to vacation in Sordland when Lespia is right there. But I suppose our country has a certain charm."

80.speaker: Symon Holl
80.text: "In addition to bringing in needed revenue, the new laws would curb excessive drinking and smoking in Sordland."

84.speaker: Gus Manger
84.text: "Some excitement around the Palace lately, I've heard."

86.speaker: Player
86.text: "That's how it is around here. A new adventure every day."

87.speaker: Player
87.text: "Don't worry about it, Gus. Focus on your job."

88.speaker: Player
88.text: "This should be a lesson to everyone. Double-cross me, and you'll pay the price."

89.speaker: Player
89.text: "The real excitement is yet to come, believe me."

90.speaker: Narrator
90.text: Gus and Symon exchanged worried looks.

91.speaker: Gus Manger
91.text: "I'm sure you're handling it very well."

95.speaker: Gus Manger
95.text: "You both know how revitalizing the Gruni region has always been my pet project of sorts."

96.speaker: Symon Holl
96.text: "Thanks for joining us, Gus. I believe you wanted to update the President on the latest developments in the Gruni region?"

98.speaker: Gus Manger
98.text: "Yes, you both know how revitalizing the region has always been my pet project of sorts."

102.speaker: Gus Manger
102.text: "Well. Thanks to the efforts of my ministry and the wise allocation of funding on the President's part, it looks like the project has finally found success."

106.speaker: Gus Manger
106.text: "Well. Thanks to the efforts of my ministry and the funding allocated by the President, Gruni is looking stable these days."

109.speaker: Gus Manger
109.text: "Well. I'm saddened to say that despite my ministry's best efforts, we're going to have to close the books on this project."

110.speaker: Symon Holl
110.text: "'Close the books', Mr. Manger? What does that mean?"

112.speaker: Gus Manger
112.text: "It means that without a massive injection of funding, the economic growth I had hoped to see in the region is simply not going to happen during this term."

113.speaker: Gus Manger
113.text: "It's far from the massive surge in economic growth that I had hoped to see. But I still believe the area has a wealth of untapped potential."

114.speaker: Symon Holl
114.text: "I've been keeping an eye on Gruni as well, of course. And it does seem to be experiencing a surge in economic growth."

116.speaker: Gus Manger
116.text: "Wine production, shipping, agriculture... the investments are pouring in. I'd call this turnaround a beacon of success for our administration."

117.speaker: Gus Manger
117.text: "This is everything I'd hoped to see at the start of our term and more."

118.speaker: Player
118.text: "Well, don't celebrate too early. The term isn't over yet."

119.speaker: Player
119.text: "Congratulations, Gus. I know how much this project meant to you."

120.speaker: Player
120.text: "That's fantastic news. It shows what can be accomplished when the president, cabinet and Assembly all work together."

121.speaker: Player
121.text: "It seems to me like my remaining time in office would be better spent focusing on other regions."

122.speaker: Player
122.text: "Terrific. Gruni is the breadbasket of Sordland. Its success will benefit us all."

123.speaker: Player
123.text: "Well, keep at it. I know how much Gruni means to you."

124.speaker: Player
124.text: "All right. I'll see what I can do to help boost development there."

125.speaker: Player
125.text: "You can't just give up. I know how much Gruni means to you."

126.speaker: Player
126.text: "I knew it from the beginning. It made no sense to try to turn Gruni into something it wasn't."

127.speaker: Player
127.text: "Perhaps this wouldn't be happening if you'd focused as much attention on Gruni as you have on your side ventures."

128.speaker: Gus Manger
128.text: "What could have been a beacon of success for Sordland is turning into a cesspool of crime, unemployment and homelessness."

130.speaker: Gus Manger
130.text: "If Gruni is failing, it is not for my lack of trying. You have no idea how much blood, sweat and tears I put into my development plan."

131.speaker: Gus Manger
131.text: "I still believe it's brimming with untapped potential. It saddens me to no end to see that go to waste."

132.speaker: Symon Holl
132.text: "Try to calm down, Gus. The President makes decisions on behalf of the entire country, not only your home region."

136.speaker: Symon Holl
136.text: "In any case, I've heard that United Contana is preparing to offer us a substantial agricultural aid package."

137.speaker: Symon Holl
137.text: "I'm suspicious, of course, but perhaps their funding can turn Gruni around where our efforts did not."

138.speaker: Gus Manger
138.text: "Not just to me, Mr. President. It's the breadbasket of this nation."

139.speaker: Gus Manger
139.text: "That would be great, Mr. President. I only hope it's not too late."

141.speaker: Gus Manger
141.text: "It's a self-fulfilling prophecy, Mr. President. If Gruni is neglected, of course it will fail."

142.speaker: Symon Holl
142.text: "I'll be on the lookout for further opportunities to invest in the region."

146.speaker: Symon Holl
146.text: "Apropos, I've heard that United Contana is preparing to offer us a substantial agricultural aid package."

147.speaker: Symon Holl
147.text: "I'm suspicious, of course, but accepting their offer could send development in Gruni through the roof."

148.speaker: Gus Manger
148.text: "That's true. But it's safe to say we're on the right track."

149.speaker: Gus Manger
149.text: "Not just to me, Mr. President. To all of Sordland."

150.speaker: Gus Manger
150.text: "We've managed to do what Soll and Alphonso couldn't."

151.speaker: Gus Manger
151.text: "Exactly. Thank you for believing in its potential."

152.speaker: Player
152.text: "I'm suspicious as well. I'm sure they'll want something in exchange."

153.speaker: Player
153.text: "Ah. Our alliance with Valgsland is already paying off."

160.speaker: Player
160.text: "It worked out well when we accepted their help before."

161.speaker: Player
161.text: "It was a mistake accepting aid from them before. I won't do so again."

162.speaker: Player
162.text: "It gladdens my heart that our comrades are willing to lend a helping hand."

164.speaker: Gus Manger
164.text: "First you accept Contanan aid, next they spark an uprising against hardworking landowners like my family."

165.speaker: Gus Manger
165.text: "If we seize every possible opportunity to invest in Gruni now, we could still see positive results within our term."

166.speaker: Gus Manger
166.text: "Not just to me, Mr. President. It's the breadbasket of this nation."

167.speaker: Gus Manger
167.text: "Gruni is the green heart of this nation, Mr. President."

171.speaker: Gus Manger
171.text: "I won't deny Gruni needs the money. But there's got to be another way."

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: The door to the White Room opened slowly, and Deivid made his way in.
172.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Decision_Turn05_SPAid_AcceptUnitedContana"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Valgsland_Alliance"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Economy_Gruni_LightTowerRegion"] == true)

174.speaker: Deivid Wisci
174.text: "Oh, hello, gentlemen. I'm early again, aren't I?"

175.speaker: Symon Holl
175.text: "Not to worry, Mr. Wisci. We've just about wrapped things up."

179.speaker: Symon Holl
179.text: "While we're both here, we may as well talk about the economic impact of our recent alliance."

180.speaker: Deivid Wisci
180.text: "A wise idea, Mr. Holl. Our new partnership is not without its consequences."

184.speaker: Deivid Wisci
184.text: "As you may recall, almost immediately after we sealed our alliance with Lespia, Valgsland imposed strict tariffs on us in retaliation."

185.speaker: Symon Holl
185.text: "The fallout won't impact our economy right away, but I do expect a significant hit before the end of the term."

186.speaker: Deivid Wisci
186.text: "As you may recall, almost immediately after we sealed our alliance with Valgsland, Lespia imposed strict tariffs on us in retaliation."

187.speaker: Deivid Wisci
187.text: "Fortunately, I believe any short-term economic harm imparted by these tariffs will be offset by the alliance's long-term benefits."

189.speaker: Player
189.text: "I wouldn't have agreed to the alliance if I didn't believe that as well. I'm looking at the big picture."

190.speaker: Player
190.text: "What if I break off the alliance? Will the tariffs end?"

191.speaker: Narrator
191.text: Symon raised an eyebrow. He gestured for Deivid to answer.

192.speaker: Deivid Wisci
192.text: "The diplomatic chaos caused by ending our alliance would dent our economy far more than these tariffs will, Mr. President."

196.speaker: Symon Holl
196.text: "I fully expect our partnership with Lespia to pay off. Arcasia has already taken notice and is planning on sending us a generous aid offer."

197.speaker: Symon Holl
197.text: "I'm not fully convinced the Valgsland partnership will pay off. Although the aid offer from United Contana is a head start."
197.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Lespia_Alliance"] == true) == false) and (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Lespia_Alliance"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Valgsland_Alliance"] == true)

198.speaker: Deivid Wisci
198.text: "Although I've heard that aid will be military in nature, which raises questions about their real motivations."

199.speaker: Narrator
199.text: Symon and Gus rose from their seats and left the room.
199.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Diplomacy_LespiaTradeTariffs"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Situation_Diplomacy_ValgslandTradeTariffs"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Lespia_Alliance"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Valgsland_Alliance"] == true) == false)

201.speaker: Deivid Wisci
201.text: "Yes, and a sign of possible greater interest from the CSP."

204.speaker: Symon Holl
204.text: "They're clearly gauging our interests in joining ATO. Which, from a purely financial standpoint, would be a great move."

205.speaker: Symon Holl
205.text: "We'll leave you to your meeting, gentlemen. My regards to Mr. Vectern."

208.speaker: Player
208.text: "Have a good afternoon, both of you."

209.speaker: Narrator
209.text: After the door closed, Deivid regarded me for a second. His blue eyes seemed to see right through me.

213.speaker: Deivid Wisci
213.text: "My ministry was notified about the Rumburgian infiltrator."

214.speaker: Deivid Wisci
214.text: "This is a very delicate situation, Anton."

215.speaker: Player
215.text: "What's delicate about it? They sent us a sex spy. They'll have to answer for it."

216.speaker: Player
216.text: "I understand. Our relations with Rumburg were precarious enough before this."

217.speaker: Player
217.text: "You don't have to tell me that."

218.speaker: Deivid Wisci
218.text: "How are you, Anton? You look as if you haven't slept in ages."

219.speaker: Player
219.text: "It's been a rough few days, Deivid."

220.speaker: Player
220.text: "Sleeplessness comes part and parcel with this job. You know that."

222.speaker: Player
222.text: "Can I ask you a personal question? Were you ever unfaithful to Cathrin?"

224.speaker: Deivid Wisci
224.text: "I've met many a beautiful woman in the course of my travels. But no, even in my younger days, I was never tempted to stray."

225.speaker: Deivid Wisci
225.text: "My deep love for my wife -- as well as the need to protect my reputation as a statesman -- prevented me from doing so."

226.speaker: Deivid Wisci
226.text: "Why? Have you broken your vows with Monica, Anton?"

227.speaker: Player
227.text: "This isn't about me. This is about Petr."

229.speaker: Player
229.text: "No. Although God knows I've thought about it."

230.speaker: Player
230.text: "Never. I love my wife more than anything."

232.speaker: Deivid Wisci
232.text: "Some thoughts are better off not translated into actions."

234.speaker: Deivid Wisci
234.text: "Some men go their entire lives without finding what you and I have. Best not to mess it up."

236.speaker: Deivid Wisci
236.text: "Men of our stature are granted a certain power in society. Some know how to wield it responsibly, and others do not."

237.speaker: Deivid Wisci
237.text: "I see that Mr. Vectern wants to do right by his wife and his position. I hope someday he finds the strength to face his demons."

238.speaker: Deivid Wisci
238.text: "Yes, we should leave this topic for another day."

239.speaker: Deivid Wisci
239.text: "I'll be very brief. Perhaps we can even carve out some time for you to rest your eyes."

240.speaker: Deivid Wisci
240.text: "But let's have this conversation over tea, not during a cabinet meeting."

241.speaker: Deivid Wisci
241.text: "I'm very glad to report that our diplomatic efforts with Rumburg have been met with an equally diplomatic response from the Kingdom."

246.speaker: Deivid Wisci
246.text: "We may even be able to enter peace talks with the Queen very soon."

247.speaker: Deivid Wisci
247.text: "Regretfully, tensions are continuing to mount between Sordland and Rumburg."

248.speaker: Deivid Wisci
248.text: "As you might imagine, our decision to grant asylum to their whistleblower Mr. Hailstone did not sit well with the Kingdom."

252.speaker: Deivid Wisci
252.text: "As you might imagine, the embargo we decreed has not been sitting well with the Kingdom."

257.speaker: Deivid Wisci
257.text: "We must exercise caution. The slightest provocation on either side could cost us our chance at reconciliation."

258.speaker: Deivid Wisci
258.text: "The tensions between Sordland and Rumburg have not eased. Quite the contrary."

259.speaker: Deivid Wisci
259.text: "As you might imagine, our decision to grant asylum to their whistleblower Mr. Hailstone did not sit well with the Kingdom."

263.speaker: Deivid Wisci
263.text: "As you might imagine, the embargo we decreed has not been sitting well with the Kingdom."

268.speaker: Deivid Wisci
268.text: "An incident such as this might serve as a tipping point. Place too much blame on Rumburg, and we may lose our chance at reconciliation."

272.speaker: Deivid Wisci
272.text: "Prior to this revelation, our diplomatic efforts with Rumburg had been met with an equally diplomatic response."

273.speaker: Deivid Wisci
273.text: "In fact, there were indications that the Kingdom would soon be ready to begin peace talks."

274.speaker: Player
274.text: "Bringing Rumburg to justice for what it's done is far more important than reconciliation."

275.speaker: Deivid Wisci
275.text: "But we must exercise caution. The slightest provocation on either side could cost us our chance at reconciliation."

276.speaker: Player
276.text: "You're right as usual. The last thing we want is a war on our hands."

277.speaker: Player
277.text: "I don't even know if peace is possible after so many years of animosity."

278.speaker: Deivid Wisci
278.text: "There is always hope for peace. No matter what."

279.speaker: Deivid Wisci
279.text: "The quest for 'justice' has blinded many a leader over the centuries. Don't let it cloud your eyes."

280.speaker: Deivid Wisci
280.text: "A compromise in the name of the greater good may spare countless lives."

281.speaker: Narrator
281.text: A pair of loud, precise raps came on the door.

287.speaker: Iosef Lancea
287.text: "For better or for worse, we are now in a military alliance with the Republic of Valgsland."

288.speaker: Deivid Wisci
288.text: "That would be General Lancea with a further update on the Valgsland alliance. If you don't mind, I'll stay for that."

289.speaker: Player
289.text: "Of course, Deivid. It's always valuable having you around."

290.speaker: Player
290.text: "A military update on Valgsland? I think I have an idea what this could be about."

291.speaker: Player
291.text: "I'm already starting to wonder whether that alliance was a good idea."

292.speaker: Narrator
292.text: Iosef brusquely entered and took a seat facing me. He and Deivid nodded at each other.

293.speaker: Narrator
293.text: He paused, as if he couldn't bring himself to go on. Finally, he continued.

294.speaker: Iosef Lancea
294.text: "As I expected, the commies -- Valgslandians -- began asking for our assistance practically as soon as the ink was dry."

295.speaker: Iosef Lancea
295.text: "Sordland's recognition of Heljiland as Valgish territory has emboldened the Republic to begin planning its invasion of the island."

296.speaker: Iosef Lancea
296.text: "Their war minister has informed me that it will commence in the coming months."

297.speaker: Player
297.text: "And? What role is Sordland expected to play in this invasion?"

298.speaker: Player
298.text: "Time for our armies to practice shooting Agnolians."

299.speaker: Player
299.text: "I hope they're not planning anything too drastic."

300.speaker: Player
300.text: "Good. I'm happy to help our brothers-in-arms claim their rightful land."

302.speaker: Iosef Lancea
302.text: "There'll be no need for that, thankfully."

303.speaker: Iosef Lancea
303.text: "If they are, they're leaving us out of it."

304.speaker: Iosef Lancea
304.text: "Thankfully, they're not asking us to play an active role."

305.speaker: Iosef Lancea
305.text: "We are readying our forces for assistance with aerial reconnaissance and a naval blockade. But our troops will not set foot on the island itself."

306.speaker: Deivid Wisci
306.text: "I too expected that allying with Valgsland would necessitate our involvement in the Heljiland situation. I'm grateful that's as far as it goes."

307.speaker: Iosef Lancea
307.text: "The Valgs had better not back down if it comes to war between Sordland and Rumburg, that's for sure."

308.speaker: Player
308.text: "Our Valgish comrades will surely come to our aid."

309.speaker: Deivid Wisci
309.text: "I'll leave you to it, Anton. I know you've got a lot on your plate."

311.speaker: Player
311.text: "Thanks for your brevity. Have a good day."

313.speaker: Narrator
313.text: Deivid left the White Room, gently closing the door behind him.

315.speaker: Player
315.text: "I hope you will not let your personal feelings about the Republic of Valgsland undermine this alliance, General."

316.speaker: Player
316.text: "This alliance was not my first choice either. But I do trust Valgsland to provide assistance if we're in need."

323.speaker: Iosef Lancea
323.text: "Comrades, eh? You're starting to sound like them."

324.speaker: Iosef Lancea
324.text: "Of course not, Mr. President. Sordland's allies are my own."

325.speaker: Deivid Wisci
325.text: "They could prove to be a formidable ally indeed."

327.speaker: Deivid Wisci
327.text: "If that's all, Mr. Lancea, I suggest we leave President Rayne to it. It's been a long morning."

334.speaker: Iosef Lancea
334.text: "Hope you tear those Rumburgians a new one for installing a damn spy in your office."

336.speaker: Player
336.text: "They'll get what's coming to them. Don't worry."

339.speaker: Narrator
339.text: My ministers left. Deivid gently closed the door behind them, allowing me a moment of quiet once more.

342.speaker: Narrator
342.text: Paskal walked in next. He didn't bother taking a seat.

343.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
343.text: "Mr. President. Only a brief update from me today."

344.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
344.text: "My ministry has been working on a pair of bills that will soon go to the Assembly."

348.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
348.text: "The first is a measure to provide state benefits to all citizens who are forced to miss work due to long-term illness or disability."

349.speaker: Player
349.text: "That's a good idea, Paskal. Those people have enough to worry about without fearing for their financial security."

350.speaker: Player
350.text: "Aren't you afraid that will lead to more workers going on indefinite 'sick leave' for made-up reasons?"

351.speaker: Player
351.text: "It should be up to companies to pay those workers' salaries. Not the government."

353.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
353.text: "Ideally, perhaps, but not all companies -- especially small businesses -- can afford such generosity."

354.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
354.text: "This measure would ensure every sick or disabled employee has access to equal benefits without disincentivizing businesses from hiring those employees."

355.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
355.text: "This doesn't seem to have happened in other countries that introduced such measures, Mr. President."

356.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
356.text: "Exactly, Mr. President. Receiving these benefits may even help them recover and get back to work faster."

357.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
357.text: "The second is called the Children for Future Act. It would provide direct financial support for low-income families with children, while ensuring that the children of unemployed parents have access to education and healthcare."

358.speaker: Player
358.text: "Very good. Children are indeed our future, even if they are not born into wealth."

359.speaker: Player
359.text: "So you're advocating we *pay* our poorest citizens to reproduce. What could go wrong with that?"

360.speaker: Player
360.text: "These seem like quite lavish expenditures, Paskal."

361.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
361.text: "The aim is for all children to have a chance to thrive, regardless of their background."

362.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
362.text: "Yes, every child deserves a chance to thrive, regardless of background."

363.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
363.text: "For a Sordland where every child is given a chance to thrive regardless of background, it will be worth it."

364.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
364.text: "Look for these measures to cross your desk soon. Assuming they're approved by the Assembly, of course."

365.speaker: Paskal Beniwoll
365.text: "We will discuss everything else in more detail during our upcoming annual health report."

369.speaker: Narrator
369.text: Paskal nodded and exited the room.

374.speaker: Iosef Lancea
374.text: "Our military alliance has emboldened the Republic to begin planning its invasion of the island."

375.speaker: Player
375.text: "I never promised to support their invasion. Tell them we will provide no support."

376.speaker: Iosef Lancea
376.text: "Of course not. Thankfully, they're not asking us to play an active role."

380.speaker: Symon Holl
